C.note: Runs the remaining command line verbatim and returns to its caller

D.note: Suppresses startup date/time input while a new permanent interpreter begins processing commands

E.note: Both 160 and 32768 byte bounds, adjacent rejections, duplication, and an observable 160-versus-512 environment-capacity difference are asserted

F.note: Automatically chooses Fail for an actual INT 24h error from an unformatted B: disk and continues without input

MSG.note: Without /P the required relationship is diagnosed; with /P resident messages are accepted by the live permanent shell

P.note: A child permanent interpreter ignores EXIT, executes the following redirected command, and never returns to its parent batch

BREAK.note: Query plus ON/OFF state transitions are asserted

CALL.note: A nested batch runs and returns to its caller

CD.note: The short form changes and reports the current directory; missing and excess paths are rejected with the prior directory preserved

CHCP.note: The default page is queried exactly and configured page 850 is selected and reported

CHDIR.note: The long form reaches the shared directory-change implementation and reports the resulting path

CLS.note: The exact ESC[2J console clear sequence is asserted

COPY.note: Ordinary, verified, concatenated, wildcard, ASCII, and binary copies assert resulting bytes; self-copy and missing-source failures preserve prior data, a missing later concatenation member is skipped, destination mode interactions are byte-exact on real DOS, and missing, excess, duplicate, and unknown syntax requires exact diagnostics

CTTY.note: CTTY AUX redirects a complete live batch session to serial output

DATE.note: Prompt-and-empty input is covered; a valid date is set and reported exactly, while an impossible calendar date is rejected before empty input returns

DEL.note: Single-file and wildcard deletion are asserted through absence; /P decline preserves a file, while duplicate /P is rejected exactly

DIR.note: Normal, wide /W, and paginated /P listings expose expected entries; duplicate and unknown switches require exact parser errors

ECHO.note: Text, blank-line, OFF, ON, and batch-suppression behavior is asserted

ERASE.note: The long synonym removes a real file; /P accept deletes exactly one selected file and an unknown switch is rejected exactly

EXIT.note: COMMAND /C EXIT returns successfully to its caller

FOR.note: A batch loop expands and visits every item exactly by marker

GOTO.note: A label jump reaches its target and skips intervening output

IF.note: EXIST, string, ERRORLEVEL, and NOT variants assert both true and false branches

LH.note: The DOS 5 alias loads COM and EXE children into a UMB, falls back low without a provider or sufficient upper space, and restores the caller's UMB link and allocation strategy

LOADHIGH.note: COM and EXE placement, child-visible upper-first strategy, conventional environment ownership, fallback, missing operands and programs, aliases, and DOS=HIGH coexistence are asserted

MD.note: The short form creates ordinary and nested directories; existing targets and excess operands are rejected without disturbing contents

MKDIR.note: The long form creates a directory observed through IF EXIST and reaches the shared validated implementation

PATH.note: Display, assignment, and clearing of the executable search path are asserted

PAUSE.note: The prompt is displayed and a supplied key resumes the batch

PROMPT.note: Prompt assignment persists in the live environment across repeated changes

RD.note: The short form removes an empty directory; non-empty and excess forms are rejected while the contained payload remains

REM.note: A remark is ignored and subsequent batch execution continues

REN.note: The short form renames a file with exact payload preservation; missing source and excess operands have exact diagnostics

RENAME.note: The long form renames normally; real DOS rejects an existing target and preserves both exact payloads, guarding against kvikdos host-rename replacement semantics

RMDIR.note: The long form removes an empty directory and reaches the shared non-empty validation path

SET.note: Environment listing, assignment, and removal are observed across one live batch; missing or repeated equals signs are rejected, and /E capacity exhaustion is behaviorally distinct

SHIFT.note: A shifted batch parameter resolves to the following argument

TIME.note: Prompt-and-empty input is covered; hours, minutes, seconds, and ticking hundredths are set and reported, while an out-of-range hour is rejected deterministically

TRUENAME.note: A path is resolved to its canonical absolute spelling

TYPE.note: Exact file payload is emitted; missing and excess filespecs require exact diagnostics

VER.note: The built command interpreter reports the exact MS-DOS 5.00 identity

VERIFY.note: Query plus ON/OFF state transitions are asserted

VOL.note: Volume information is obtained from the active drive; unavailable and excess drive forms require exact diagnostics
